commits.message:
fix(strip): an arrow is drawn in its left ground as drawn, and measured as the writer draws it

Style.drawnColors is the one account of the colours a style puts on screen;
toSgrCodes encodes exactly those, and the joiner measures its arrow through
them, so a translucent ground is not composited a second time over the
ground the arrow enters.

feat(color): floors hold on the colours drawn — the strip's seam, ansi text, and ensureDrawn

- RenderOptions.colorSystem: the depth the output is encoded at, set by
  renderToString and Console, so a renderable can measure what it draws
- PowerlineJoiner decides arrow or divider on the drawn colours: two grounds
  256 colours or ANSI draw as one are one ground, and the divider sits on the
  left item's own ground, so it reads exactly as that item's text
- ensureContrast at ANSI: text never lands on its background's index
- ensureDrawn(chosen, drawnAt, accept): the nearest drawable colour a stated
  floor accepts, for floors that are not text on a background
- ColorSpec.fixedValue, ColorTable.matchWhere

fix(color): contrast is chosen against a translucent background as drawn (#156)
